name: Zillow Group, Inc.

profile.description: Zillow Group, Inc. operates the most-visited US residential real estate marketplace, monetizing through Premier Agent and For Sale services, Rentals (including multifamily), and Zillow Home Loans. Under CEO Jeremy Wacksman (CEO since 2024, at Zillow since 2009) the company is pursuing a 'housing super app' strategy and calls itself an AI-native company, launching 'AI Mode' in 2026. Q2 2026 revenue rose 18% to $772M, with Rentals up 31% and Mortgages up 75%; Q3 2026 guidance is $745-760M with results due November 4, 2026. Market cap approximately $7.0B at $30.96.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): After exiting iBuying, Zillow built new revenue streams in rentals and mortgages; Q2 2026 Rentals revenue rose 31% to $209M (multifamily +42%) and Mortgages rose 75% to $84M on a 95% jump in purchase originations [1][2]. AI Deployment (2/2): Zillow has shipped machine learning for years through the Zestimate and listing computer vision, and in 2026 launched AI Mode, a personalized assistant that remembers mover preferences across sessions; Wacksman says employees have been retrained to use AI and productivity has risen [4][5]. Market Share (2/2): Zillow is the category-defining US home-search portal, and its Listing Access Standards survived a Compass antitrust challenge when the court denied a preliminary injunction [6]. Product Pipeline (1/2): The housing super app and AI Mode rollout are clearly described, but there are no dated product launches with revenue targets [5]. R&D Intensity (1/1): FY2025 R&D of $607M was 23.5% of $2.58B revenue, top-quartile for internet marketplaces [3].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): Zillow's purpose of helping people get home is specific and service-oriented and has guided its move from a listings site toward a full-transaction platform over 20 years [4]. Community Impact (0/2): No distinctive charitable program with dollar amounts was found in research. Employee Retention (0/2): No retention data was found; the company is retraining staff around AI [4]. Insider Buying (0/2): FMP insider data shows no open-market purchases and about 100 insider sales over the last four quarters (12 in Q3 2026, 21 in Q2, 29 in Q1, 38 in Q4 2025) [7].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Calculated mechanically using the Growth weighting (10 weight units). Debt-to-equity of 13.0% (1.0), revenue growth of 17.9% YoY (1.0), forward P/E of 11.2 (1.0) and the provider-reported PEG of 0.93 (1.0 at 2x) all hit target [8]. The 5-year revenue CAGR of 9.7% (FMP revenue of $1.624B in 2020, restated for continuing operations, to $2.583B in 2025) scores 0.98 at 2x [3]. Profitability is the weak spot: ROE of 1.2% scores 0.08 at 2x and profit margin of 2.0% scores 0.10 [8]. Weighted sum 7.22 / 10, rounded to 7. Net cash is positive at $698M cash against $558M debt, and free cash flow is $244M [8]. Liquidity floor cleared: 4.14M avg daily volume x $30.96 = about $128M.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (5/9): Zillow's core is consumer traffic that it sells to agents, which is exactly the layer AI assistants could intermediate. Management rejects the 'AI flattens agents' narrative and argues its edge is proprietary data that compounds across the whole transaction, but the sources available mostly repeat company messaging and do not independently test whether ChatGPT-style search erodes portal traffic [4][5]. The stock's fall from a 52-week high of $77.07 to $30.96 shows the market is pricing meaningful risk to the model [8]. AI Opportunity (0/1): AI Mode and AI-driven productivity gains are real, but Zillow has not disclosed any revenue attributable to AI products [5].

infinite_game.summary: Zillow has a durable consumer purpose and a CEO who has been inside the company for 17 years, which gives it continuity few internet companies have. Its biggest strategic swing, iBuying, ended in a costly retreat in 2021, and its current competitive posture is litigation: defending its listing rules against Compass and suing Compass and MRED in return. Seen through Sinek's lens, the cause is real but the competitive mindset is finite.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Helping people get home has outlasted the shift from founder Rich Barton to Wacksman and connects the listings, rentals and mortgage businesses in the super app strategy [4]. The iBuying episode showed the cause can be pursued through strategies that failed, so it is not yet a proven competitive advantage.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Leadership continuity is strong; Wacksman joined in 2009 and rose to CEO in 2024 [4]. The company is retraining staff around AI rather than replacing them, but there is no independent retention data, and the 2021 iBuying wind-down cut about a quarter of the workforce.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Zillow's relationship with Compass has become legal warfare: it defended its Listing Access Standards against Compass's antitrust suit, then in May 2026 sued MRED and Compass, alleging a group boycott [6]. That is competing to win, not to learn.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Zillow has shown it can change course by exiting iBuying and rebuilding around rentals, mortgages and an AI-native super app [2][5]. The iBuying exit was forced by losses rather than chosen in service of the cause.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Zillow took a costly public stand against private 'hidden' listings, risking relationships with the largest brokerage, and is putting R&D (23.5% of revenue) into AI during a weak housing market [3][6]. Whether that stance is principled or self-serving is open to debate.

investment_thesis: Zillow is growing well above the housing market. Q2 2026 revenue rose 18% to $772M, above the top of guidance, with For Sale up 14%, Rentals up 31% and Mortgages up 75% on a 95% rise in purchase originations [1][2]. The business has turned GAAP-profitable (FY2025 net income $23M versus a $112M loss in 2024), carries more cash than debt, and generates $244M of free cash flow [3][8]. At a forward P/E of 11.2 and a PEG of 0.93, with a consensus target of $41.17, the shares price in little of the super app strategy, and Q3 results on November 4 against $745-760M guidance are a near-term catalyst [1][8].
thesis_continued: The bear case is that AI assistants and listing-access fights threaten the traffic monopoly that funds everything else. The stock has fallen about 60% from its 52-week high of $77.07, ROE is only 1.2%, and the trailing P/E is 135 [8]. Litigation with Compass and MRED is ongoing and could restrict listing data, and insiders have sold steadily with no open-market buying over the past year [6][7]. Management guides Q4 residential growth only in line with the purchase mortgage industry, so a stalled housing market would cap growth [1].
key_catalysts: Q3 2026 results on November 4 against $745-760M revenue guidance, compared with $676M in Q3 2025 [1]
Rentals (+31%, multifamily +42%) and Zillow Home Loans (+75%) scaling into a larger share of revenue in the housing super app [2]
AI Mode adoption raising engagement and agent conversion, in line with management's 'AI-native company' claims [4][5]
key_risks: AI search and chat assistants pulling home-search traffic away from portals, weakening the agent lead-generation model [4][5]
Antitrust litigation with Compass and MRED over listing standards could limit Zillow's access to listings data [6]
Thin profitability (1.2% ROE, 2.0% margin) leaves earnings exposed to a prolonged housing slowdown [8]
